children: Shares of offshore services provider Oceaneering International
fell 17.5% in the afternoon session after the company reported a 26% year-over-year decline in net income attributable to the company for the third quarter of 2026.

According to a company press release, Oceaneering reported third-quarter revenue of $784.6 million, operating income of $92.2 million, and net income attributable to the company of $52.6 million. Adjusted earnings per share was 50 cents, which was below analysts' expectations of 59 cents. Revenue rose 5.6% year over year and was above Wall Street's estimate of $780.6 million, while adjusted EBITDA of $119.4 million was above expectations of $117.4 million. The release also said that fourth-quarter free cash flow generation would moderate due to seasonality and project mix shifts, following strong operational cash flow during the third quarter. Additionally, the company introduced full-year 2027 EBITDA guidance between $430 million and $480 million.
What is the market telling us

Oceaneering’s shares are very volatile and have had 22 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Oceaneering and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 3 months ago when the stock gained 8.2% on the news that the company reported strong second-quarter earnings, with EPS and revenue beating Wall Street's expectations. Taking a closer look at the results, revenue rose 10% year-on-year to $768.2 million. Adjusted earnings per share outperformed estimates by 40% at $0.63. Adjusted EBITDA reached $114.5 million, beating Wall Street's estimates by 8.5%. The company also generated a 14.9% EBITDA margin, in line with the same quarter last year, indicating its overall cost structure has been relatively stable. Overall, it was a solid quarter, with rising top and bottom lines contributing to the stock's strong performance.

Oceaneering is up 45.7% since the beginning of the year, but at $36.20 per share, it is still trading 33.1% below its 52-week high of $54.11 from August 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Oceaneering’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,351.
